app/app/lib/data.server.ts:1 — `.server.ts` suffix keeps the API client and its cache out of client bundles (documented convention)

churn_resistance.rationale: Structurally well set up to survive framework churn: one data module, `.server.ts` isolation, no internals relied on, config in single files, so an 8→9 upgrade (no future flags currently required) would touch almost nothing. But the complete absence of types at the loader/component/data boundaries is exactly where future requirement changes (new API fields, overlay data differences the tests exercise) will bite, and the not-found logic is triplicated.

findings.issue: No route-module type generation is used: every loader is typed `loader({ request }: any)` and every component `({ loaderData }: any)` (home.tsx:110, pokemon.tsx:142/292, type.tsx:26/59, move.tsx:22/54, ability.tsx), despite tsconfig.json being fully scaffolded with rootDirs and a `react-router typegen && tsc` typecheck script.
findings.suggestion: Import `type { Route } from "./+types/<route>"` in each route module and use `Route.LoaderArgs`, `Route.MetaArgs`, `Route.ComponentProps`, per reactrouter.com/explanation/type-safety — this also types loaderData end-to-end for free.

findings.issue: Missing resources return `{ notFound: true }` from loaders (also type.tsx:31, pokemon.tsx:144, ability.tsx), so responses are HTTP 200 and the documented flow — `throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 })` rendered by the route/root ErrorBoundary (reactrouter.com/how-to/status) — is bypassed.
findings.suggestion: Throw `data("Not Found", { status: 404 })` and let the existing root ErrorBoundary render it; this removes the per-route NotFound component, the notFound flag in every loader return, and the special-case in every meta function.

findings.issue: The entire API boundary is untyped: getList/getResource/getByUrl return `Promise<any>` and format.ts helpers accept `resource: any`, so the domain layer the tests mutate via live-data-overlay has no compile-time contract.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI shapes used (NamedAPIResource, Pokemon, Species, Move, Type…) in one place and have the data module return them; keeps the boundary typed even before route typegen is adopted.

findings.issue: HashScroller re-implements hash-anchor scrolling with two setTimeout retries (0 ms and 100 ms), duplicating what <ScrollRestoration> (root.tsx:38) already does on client navigations and the browser does on initial load.
findings.suggestion: Delete HashScroller and rely on ScrollRestoration; if extra settling time is genuinely needed after data loads, keep it as a comment explaining why rather than a blind double-timer.

findings.issue: Search text lives in two sources of truth (URL query and useState) synced by a useEffect that overwrites local state whenever the URL changes (home.tsx:117-119), a pattern prone to lost keystrokes and re-render churn when filters change the URL.
findings.suggestion: Derive the input value from useSearchParams directly (or a single reducer keyed off searchParams), or wrap the selects in a `<Form method="get">` as the framework-mode docs recommend for filter forms.

findings.issue: isbot is declared as a dependency but never imported — it is only used by a custom entry.server.tsx, which this app doesn't have (the framework's default entry doesn't consume it).
findings.suggestion: Remove isbot; re-add it only if a custom entry.server.tsx is introduced.

findings.issue: @react-router/node is never imported; the only runtime use is via react-router-serve, and @react-router/serve@8.5.1 already depends on @react-router/node directly.
findings.suggestion: Drop the direct dependency (or keep it deliberately with a comment if pinning the version matters).

findings.issue: `resolve.tsconfigPaths` is enabled (a good, current Vite 8 feature) but no module uses the `~/` alias declared in tsconfig.json:20-22, so it's dead config.
findings.suggestion: Either use the alias for imports from app/ (e.g. `~/lib/data.server`) or remove the alias and the option.

summary: This is a clean, current React Router 8 Framework-Mode app: right version, right file layout, no deprecated APIs, and a single well-isolated server-only data module, so framework upgrades would barely ripple. Its forward-looking weaknesses are the total bypass of the +types route type generation (every loader/component is `any`, despite the scaffold being wired for it), a hand-rolled not-found flag instead of the documented throw-data(404) flow, and two dead template dependencies. Solid, maintainable code that is one refactor away from exemplary.
